A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Conductor research work, with 39 readable pages and complete Appendices A–F. Text and visual comparisons establish that pages 2–39 are identical; first-page differences are cosmetic.

before.justification: v2 reports original Conductor benchmark results, recursion experiments, efficiency analyses, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains the same original experimental outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix B, including benchmark comparisons and ablations.

M1.justification: The workflow specification, GRPO training, rewards, adaptive worker selection, and recursive inference procedure in Section 3 are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training and evaluation coverage across MATH/MATH500, MMLU, RLPR, LiveCodeBench, AIME25, BigCodeBench, and GPQA-Diamond. Appendix E retains the same additional few-shot sources.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout: individual workers, context-length and self-reflection baselines, consensus, MASRouter, MoA, RouterDC, both Smoothie variants, and frontier-model conductor replacements.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain identical splits, sample counts, model configurations, training budgets, metrics, and constrained versus unconstrained evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The same model-scale, task-adaptivity, efficiency, few-shot, subtask, agent-selection, topology, and recursion analyses remain in Section 4 and Appendix B. Appendix F's qualitative examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions state that evaluations are repeated up to 16 times and report mean accuracy and standard errors. The uncertainty reporting in Table 7 is identical.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports Conductor scores of 83.93 on LiveCodeBench and 87.5 on GPQA-Diamond in both versions; Table 2 retains the recursive BigCodeBench score of 40.0.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective and advantage equations, workflow definition, and reward conditions in Sections 2–3 are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain identical claims about learned natural-language orchestration, the 7B Conductor's benchmark performance, customizable worker pools, and recursive test-time scaling.

C2.justification: Interpretations of prompt engineering, worker specialization, difficulty adaptivity, and recursive redistribution are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same explanations of baseline failures and the limited benefit of finer-grained topology control.

D1.justification: Appendices A and E retain identical hyperparameters, hardware, processing and evaluation details, prompts, and few-shot examples. The reproducibility statement and code/model access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: All cited works and bibliography entries are identical. Section 5 retains the same positioning relative to tool-using reinforcement learning and multi-agent coordination.

P1.justification: v4 changes punctuation and spacing in the first-page author block and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose, terminology, section order, and appendix structure are identical.

P2.justification: First-page typesetting changes slightly, including author-block spacing and vertical positioning of the abstract, introduction, and Figure 1. Figures and tables retain their content and design; pages 2–39 render identically.

improvement.justification: v4 introduces only cosmetic first-page edits and an updated version/date stamp. The methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
